summary_md:
**[@HEI](https://x.com/HEI/status/2115628761215344847)** (an NLP-papers feed) shares **Distill, Debate, Discover** (Ma, Liu, Kim, Liang, Callison-Burch).

Per the abstract, it tackles how to give debating research agents distinct, meaningful expertise. **InsightAgents** distills insights from graphs of related papers — how approaches evolved, hidden assumptions, open challenges — and agents then jointly pick a problem and propose, challenge and refine approaches into a research proposal, evaluated against three ideation frameworks on 100 NLP topics.

referenced_urls.title: Distill, Debate, Discover: Grounding Multi-Agent Research Ideation in Graph-Distilled Insights

relevance: Grounds multi-agent creativity in literature-derived expertise, a concrete recipe for better AI ideation.

media.description: Screenshot of the paper's abstract on a beige background.
media.ocr_text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support research idea generation and scientific discovery. Multi-agent debate offers a collaborative approach to this task by bringing together diverse perspectives to develop research ideas. However, a key challenge is how to equip agents with distinct and meaningful expertise to guide their contributions. Inspired by how researchers draw on accumulated research experience during collaboration, we introduce InsightAgents, a framework that constructs literature-grounded agent expertise by distilling insights from graphs of related papers.
